## Godwin C. Umeobi

I am a doctoral student in Psychometrics and Graduate Instructor in the Department of Psychology at Morgan State University, Baltimore, Maryland. My academic and professional interests span psychological measurement, quantitative research methods, human behavior, and the application of statistical and psychometric methods to understanding psychological and educational phenomena.

My current research focuses on **process data, response latency, and response behavior in psychological and educational assessments**, particularly in technology-mediated environments. I am interested in understanding not only the responses individuals provide to assessment items but also the underlying processes involved in producing those responses, with implications for measurement validity, data quality, and assessment interpretation.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {

  function updateVisitorDateTime() {
    const now = new Date();

    const dateElement =
      document.getElementById("visitor-date");

    const timeElement =
      document.getElementById("visitor-time");

    if (!dateElement || !timeElement) return;

    const dateOptions = {
      weekday: "long",
      year: "numeric",
      month: "long",
      day: "numeric"
    };

    const timeOptions = {
      hour: "numeric",
      minute: "2-digit",
      timeZoneName: "short"
    };

    dateElement.textContent =
      new Intl.DateTimeFormat(
        "en-US",
        dateOptions
      ).format(now);

    timeElement.textContent =
      new Intl.DateTimeFormat(
        "en-US",
        timeOptions
      ).format(now);
  }

  updateVisitorDateTime();

  setInterval(updateVisitorDateTime, 1000);

});
</script>
